Azt mondta, a kormány intézkedési terve 60 tételben sorolja fel, mire fordítják majd a hazahozott uniós pénzeket. A miniszterelnök szerint a fejlesztések megvalósulásával mindenki érezni fogja, hogy az ország fejlődik. A lakhatás terén most először indul olyan nagy, uniós program Magyarországon, amely kifejezetten megfizethető bérlakások és diákotthonok létrehozását szolgálja, erre 600 millió eurót, vagyis több mint 230 milliárd forintot fordítanak. 54 milliárd forintnyi, korábban magyar költségvetési forrásból megvalósított iskolai beruházást most uniós forrásból fognak elszámolni. Több mint 151 milliárd forintot fordítanak arra, hogy a tanulók és a pedagógusok egyenlőbben férjenek hozzá a digitális oktatáshoz. Az egészségügyre uniós forrásból közel 170 milliárd forintot fordítanak, ebből 24 milliárd megy a háziorvosi ellátás fejlesztésére. Több mint 125 milliárd forintnyi, korábban magyar költségvetésből megvalósuló egészségügyi beruházást és digitalizációs fejlesztést uniós forrásból fognak elszámolni. A miniszterelnök szerint az Orbán-kormány késlekedésének súlyos ára volt, az eredeti helyreállítási terv szerint több mint 500 milliárd forintot is kaphatott volna Magyarország egészségügyre. A közlekedésben évtizedek óta várt járműcserék lesznek, lecserélik a szentendrei, ráckevei és csepeli HÉV elöregedett, 40-50 éves szerelvényeit, helyettük 42 új, korszerű, alacsonypadlós szerelvény jön. Megújulnak a vidéki InterCityk is, 35 új, emeletes motorvonat érkezik. Több százmilliárd jut majd a magyar energiarendszer korszerűsítésére. Új korszak jön a magyar kkv-knak, 645 milliárddal erősítik meg a Magyar Fejlesztési Bankot, hogy az ilyen vállalkozásoknak több finanszírozás juthasson. „Ezek azok a lehetőségek, amelyektől az Orbán-kormány éveken keresztül megfosztotta Magyarországot.” Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Photograph: Senatobia Police Department via Facebook View image in fullscreen It was announced that Sentobia’s police chief Harold Vanderford was fired on Tuesday. Photograph: Senatobia Police Department via Facebook Mississippi Police chief in Mississippi town where 1-year-old was killed has been fired Senatobia, where white officer shot and killed Kohen Wiley, terminates chief who reportedly used racist slurs in texts Adria R Walker Wed 2 Sep 2026 15.10 EDT Last modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 15.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Late Tuesday, the city of Senatobia, Mississippi fired its police chief, Harold Vanderford, after it was reported that Vanderford regularly used racist slurs against Black people in his text messages. The town, which is about 40% Black , made national news earlier this year after a white officer fatally shot and killed Kohen Wiley , a one-year-old Black baby, while responding to a shoplifting call at Walmart. Officers fired into a vehicle, shooting the driver and killing the toddler, who was being held in his mother’s arms. Though Vanderford submitted a resignation letter earlier on 1 September, the city’s board of aldermen unanimously voted to reject it and to terminate the officer instead. Vanderford’s firing came just under a week after the city wrote in a statement that, despite the messages, he would “continue to serve the City with the confidence that was placed in him at the time that he was appointed as Chief”. Senatobia has been embroiled in recent controversies involving police and Black residents, specifically children. In 2023, Senatobia made national news after an officer arrested and placed in a cell a 10-year-old Black boy who had urinated in public. The child was later sentenced to three months’ probation. A year before Wiley was killed, at the same Walmart, an officer forced a Black woman from her car in front of her children after she parked in a handicap space to wait for her grandmother, who was shopping in the store. The woman was driving a vehicle with a handicap parking tag. Last year, the town’s elected alderman moved to replace the previous police chief who was serving at the time of the arrest of the 10-year-old with Vanderford . Angelica Maze, who is Black, has been named interim police chief. Vanderford’s firing has prompted renewed calls for transparency with Wiley’s case. State and local law enforcement have said that they will not provide updates until their investigation is complete. The toddler’s family retained the civil-rights attorney Ben Crump, who presented forensic evidence indicating that the officers had not been in harm’s way when they fired into the vehicle. An investigation found that Sgt Hunter Foster, who was identified in reports as the officer who shot the toddler, had made racist and derogatory remarks to a Black colleague just two days before the Walmart shooting. “Removing [Vanderford] was the right decision, and the Senatobia Board of Aldermen deserves credit for acting. But it does not answer the question Kohen’s family has been asking since June 14: what happened to their baby?” Crump said in a statement following Vanderford’s firing. “A 1-year-old was shot and killed by an officer of this department, and nearly three months later his family still has not been allowed to see the footage. The racist language that cost Chief Vanderford his job is exactly why this family cannot simply be told to trust the process. MBI has the footage. Release it, finish the investigation into Sgt Foster, and give this family the facts they have been owed since the day Kohen died.” The Mississippi legislative Black caucus called on the state attorney general, Lynn Fitch, and public safety commissioner, Sean Tindell, to take immediate action in Wiley’s death, demanding that the state establish “a clear point of contact and provide the family with direct, timely and ongoing updates about the investigation”. Experts: Houthi Attacks on Islamic Holy Sites Violate International Law https://english.aawsat.com/gulf/5319316-experts-houthi-attacks-islamic-holy-sites-violate-international-law Gulf Experts: Houthi Attacks on Islamic Holy Sites Violate International Law Houthi militia attacks have escalated systematically, targeting Islamic holy sites and civilian facilities in Saudi Arabia (SPA) Riyadh: Ghazi al-Harthi 07:31-17 September 2026 AD ـ 06 Rabi’ Al-Thani 1448 AH T T Riyadh: Ghazi al-Harthi 07:31-17 September 2026 AD ـ 06 Rabi’ Al-Thani 1448 AH T T Experts: Houthi Attacks on Islamic Holy Sites Violate International Law Houthi militia attacks have escalated systematically, targeting Islamic holy sites and civilian facilities in Saudi Arabia (SPA) The Houthis have continued to target Islamic holy sites, most recently with a drone attack on Makkah, while the Coalition stressed that “the security of the Two Holy Mosques is a red line.” Experts told Asharq Al-Awsat that attacks on places of worship constitute a violation of international law. Tuesday’s targeting of Makkah was not the first such attack. Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki said it followed an earlier ballistic missile attack in July 2017. The Coalition stressed that “the security of the Two Holy Mosques and the Umrah performers is a red line” and that its Joint Forces Command “will not hesitate to take the necessary and deterrent measures against the terrorist Houthi militia and its hostile and terrorist behavior.” The drone targeting Makkah, intercepted and destroyed by the Royal Saudi Air Defense Forces south of the city, marked another attack on Islamic holy sites and places of worship. It followed Saturday’s targeting of a mosque in Al-Tuwal governorate in Jazan, as well as an attack launched from Iraqi territory against Madinah. The Coalition statement said the incident “can only be described as a disgraceful act — an attempt to target the cradle of revelation, the land of the divine message and a destination cherished by millions of Muslims from around the world.” It said the attack also sought to terrorize pilgrims visiting the Grand Mosque and harm citizens and residents. “This hostile attempt will remain a black mark on the record of violations committed by the extremist terrorist Houthi militia, as it was a deliberate act intended to provoke the feelings of millions of Muslims,” the statement said. Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry condemned the attack, while several Arab and Islamic countries and other states in the region and around the world expressed solidarity. They also praised the Royal Saudi Air Defense Forces for intercepting the hostile drone before it entered restricted airspace over Makkah. Violation of International Law Under the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, intentionally directing attacks against buildings dedicated to religion, including mosques and places of worship, constitutes a war crime in international and non-international armed conflicts, provided they are not military objectives. Places of worship of cultural or spiritual importance receive additional protection under Article 53 of Additional Protocol I and Article 16 of Additional Protocol II to the Geneva Conventions. Rule 38 of customary international humanitarian law also requires particular care to avoid damage to buildings dedicated to religious purposes. Deliberate attacks on mosques and places of worship during armed conflict therefore violate international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes when the sites are not military objectives. Targeting Regional Security Dr. Khaled Al-Habbas, former Arab League assistant secretary-general for political affairs, told Asharq Al-Awsat that attacks on the Kingdom by Iran-aligned militias underscored what he described as their functional role as proxies directed by the Revolutionary Guard Corps to destabilize regional security and stability. Given Saudi Arabia’s regional and international standing and influence, its spiritual and economic importance, its position as a strategic depth for Gulf states and at the heart of the Arab and Islamic worlds, Al-Habbas argued that Iran had sought to target the Kingdom through its regional proxies. Such attacks, he maintained, amounted to targeting the security and stability of the entire region and, beyond that, regional and international security. ‘Aggression Against the Islamic World’ Al-Habbas stressed that the escalation came amid a decline in Iran’s regional role, including its ability to control the Strait of Hormuz. He described the conduct and aggression of its proxies against the Kingdom as evidence of disregard for good-neighborly relations, international law and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. Attacks on holy sites, he added, constituted a serious violation of their sanctity and “blatant aggression against all Islamic countries” that required condemnation and action. “Despite the Kingdom’s consistent approach of de-escalation and support for a political settlement, it certainly has the right to defend its security and stability,” Al-Habbas said, calling on Arab and Islamic countries to confront what he described as the arrogance and aggression of Iran and its proxies. He also urged the international community to take a firm stance against the militias, arguing that regional security was inseparable from international security because of the region’s geostrategic and economic importance. Political analyst Abdul Latif Al-Mulhim described such attacks as a continuation of what he called the Houthis’ systematic hostile approach and attacks targeting residential areas and vital facilities, in flagrant defiance of international and humanitarian laws and conventions. He argued that the attacks reflected the group’s extremist criminal conduct, its rejection of all peace efforts and a threat to regional and international security and stability. International Responsibility Al-Habbas and Al-Mulhim agreed that the attacks, coinciding with the militia’s control of the Bab Al-Mandab Strait and its imposition of restrictions on maritime navigation, offered the world and the international community a clear indication of the conduct to be expected from the group if it continued such practices. They warned of an imminent threat to the region’s security and economic future if the international community delayed fulfilling its responsibilities in combating the group’s actions. The statements described the targeting of Makkah as a grave escalation and a violation of the city’s religious sanctity, while reaffirming support for efforts to protect the holy sites and prevent further threats to regional security. Published on November 1, 2026 By Meaghan Murray Facebook Twitter Photo by Tony Webster , CC BY 2.0 On the morning of October 12, federal agents raided a house in one of Washington DC’s northeast neighborhoods. They were collecting evidence. Was it the residence of any one of the politically powerful men mentioned in the Epstein files? To date, the only two arrests have been Jeffrey Epstein and his co-trafficker, Ghislaine Maxwell. Was it the home of Kristi Noem? In the last year, she spent hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars on luxury jets—the jets, she says, would be used for deportations. Or, perhaps, it was where Pete Hegseth lived? The United Nations had recently accused the US military of committing war crimes in Iran, under Hegseth’s leadership. No. These federal agents were with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). The home they were raiding belonged to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota. HSI agents seized her phone, computer, and notebooks as part of an investigation into “immigration fraud,” predicated on claims around her marriage history and what age her father had said she was when applying for citizenship. Right-wing Retaliation The timing, the context, and the goal are clear: This search warrant was executed weeks before the midterm elections, against a Muslim woman and Somali American serving a district at the center of Operation Metro Surge, ICE’s invasion of Minnesota last winter. It came just weeks after she introduced the Make ICE Pay Act, proposing a reallocation of ICE’s budget to the communities most impacted by their terror campaigns. The Trump regime’s clear intent is to strip Omar of her citizenship and deport her, and they have launched a fishing expedition to find a pretext. But this isn’t just an attack on Ilhan Omar—this is an attack against Muslim and Somali Americans, two of those communities that have been subjected to endless racist abuse from the Trump regime. Her being one of the original members of the “Squad” also played a part, and this is certainly tied to the wave of political repression directed at the broader left in the United States. This includes the Minnesota 15 and the Righteous 39 in the Twin Cities, as well as the Michigan 8 , Spokane 3 , and the Prairieland defendants—all activists that have done what hundreds of thousands have done in the past several years; they’ve spoken out and protested against ICE and the genocide in Gaza. After the general strike in Minneapolis on January 23 and the historic actions in Minnesota’s streets over the winter, Trump is still licking his wounds and vindictive. This is just another stop on his campaign trail of vengeance. It’s a threat: No undocumented, asylum-seeking, or even naturalized American is safe if you speak out against our violent, racist, xenophobic, right-wing government. Currently, there are approximately 26 million naturalized citizens in the US. Trump has made it no secret that denaturalization is a weapon his administration will wield against anyone who commits any infraction or isn’t groveling at the feet of imperialism. Trump’s been vilifying Omar since she spoke out against the US-Israel war machine in 2019 . Now, the Justice Department has broken “time-honored norms ” by bringing forth an investigation of a sitting member of Congress within 60 days of an election. This is just one of a flurry of cases the DOJ has pushed in the last month that focus on outspoken critics of Trump. While this timing is unheard of for the modern-day Department of Justice, there is a history of denaturalization and deportation as a means to repress left-wing activists and working-class struggle in the United States. During Woodrow Wilson’s presidency, Attorney General A. Mitchell Palmer and a young J. Edgar Hoover stripped Lithuanian-born anarchist Emma Goldman of her citizenship and deported her to the Soviet Union. She was among hundreds of other foreign-born communists and anarchists who were detained and deported in what’s known as the Palmer Raids . Drop The Investigation, Stop The Repression! If only there was universal support for Ilhan Omar among House Democrats: 40 of her own Democratic colleagues did not sign the letter condemning the Trump administration’s raid and urging that the investigation be dropped. It’s unsurprising that a thoroughly corporate party would contain so many representatives who see this attack as too risky to comment on ahead of their elections. Some may even see this intimidation of a pesky left-leaning colleague as not such a bad thing. We have serious political disagreements with Omar—her commitment to working within the Democratic Party being one of them—but that doesn’t change us seeing this for what it is: A racist, Islamophobic, xenophobic, right-wing attack and an attempt to fearmonger and repress immigrants and anyone who fights alongside them. We’ve seen this one before. Socialist Alternative calls for dropping this investigation, and to drop the charges against all anti-ICE protesters and targets of political repression. As part of this fight, we call for building a mass workers’ party, one that would boldly push back against the Trump regime with methods of mass struggle—something the Democratic Party has no interest in doing because of the potential threat to their system. It’s clear that neither of the two capitalist parties have any way forward for immigrants, or for the working class as a whole. A genuine left alternative, made up of workers and young people, is what’s needed to dismantle everything Trump stands for. Latest articles US Politics What Should The Democratic Socialists Do Now?
